summary: Robert Alan Goodding works in Indology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Texas at Austin in 2002 under the supervision of Patrick Olivelle.

Robert Alexander Neil was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Aberdeen and Cambridge under E. B. Cowell and others. He served as University Lecturer in Sanskrit at Cambridge (1883–1901) and Fellow at Pembroke College.

Robert Anderson was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. Educated at Harrow School and the East India Company College, he later served as an assistant professor at the East India Company College from 1821 to 1825.

Robert Anthony Orsi is a scholar of religious studies and history. After studying at Trinity College and Yale, he held positions at Fordham, Indiana University Bloomington, Harvard (2001–2007), and Northwestern University from circa 2007.

Robert Antoine was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who earned an M.A. from the University of Calcutta. He taught Sanskrit at St. Xavier's Collegiate School (1951) and was a reader at Jadavpur University from 1956.

Robert Arrowsmith worked in linguistics and Indology. Educated at Columbia University and Berlin, he taught Latin and Sanskrit at Racine College, was a professor at Teachers College, Columbia, and served as an editor at the American Book Company (1894–1913).

Robert Atkinson was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at Trinity College Dublin and Liège. He served as Professor of Romance Languages and Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology (1871–1907) at Trinity.

Robert Baker Aitken worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Hawaiʱi and UC Berkeley, trained under several Zen masters including D. T. Suzuki, and held positions at the East-West Center and University of Hawaiʱi.
Robert Barkley Shaw was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He completed his education at Marlborough College and Trinity College, Cambridge.

Robert Barnett is a Tibetologist educated at the University of Cambridge. He served as Adjunct Professor of Contemporary Tibetan Studies at Columbia University (circa 1999–2018) and Professorial Research Associate at SOAS University of London from circa 2018.

Robert Bleichsteiner was an Austrian scholar of Tibetology, Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He earned his PhD at the University of Vienna under Bittner, von Schroeder, and Geiger, later serving there as professor and as director of Weltmuseum Wien (1945).

Robert Boxberger was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied under August Schleicher at the University of Jena. He worked as a teacher at Realschule Erfurt (1858–1876) and a librarian at the Herzogin Anna Amalia Bibliothek (1868–1876).

Robert Brainerd Ekvall was a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who studied at Wheaton, Nyack, and the University of Chicago. He held research positions at Chicago, the University of Washington, and the Burke Museum (1965–1973).

Robert Bruce Foote was an archaeologist who served as Superintendent of the Geological Survey of India (1858–1891) and later held posts in Baroda State and as Director of the Mysore Geological Department (1894).

Robert Caesar Childers was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Wadham College, Oxford, and under Yataramulle Dhammarama. He served as sub-librarian at the India Office (1872) and professor of Pali at University College London (1873).

Robert Chalmers was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Oriel College, Oxford, and under T. W. Rhys Davids. He served as president of the Royal Asiatic Society (1922–1925) and Master of Peterhouse, Cambridge (1924–1931).

Robert Chambers was an Indologist and legal scholar educated at Oxford. He served as Vinerian Professor of English Law at Oxford (1766–1777), Chief Justice of the Supreme Court at Fort William, and President of The Asiatic Society (1797–1799).

Robert Charles Zaehner was a scholar of religious, Iranian, and Indological studies. He studied at Oxford and under H. W. Bailey at Cambridge, later serving as Oxford's Spalding Professor of Eastern Religions and Ethics and Fellow of All Souls College (1952–1974).
Robert Cotton Mather was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He completed his education at the University of Edinburgh, the University of Glasgow, and Homerton College.

Robert DeCaroli is an art historian and Indologist. He earned his MA and PhD at UCLA under Robert L. Brown, and later held teaching posts at UCLA, Loyola Marymount University, and George Mason University from circa 1999.
